original_card.question: Can the native P104 low-rank channel be completed with a legal, fully charged I-G/2 side correction?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier.

first_step.inspect: Read the P104 open next questions and its fixed local histogram; inspect why appending I-G/2 after source completion is not justified. #1991 supplies the checked native channel, not the missing correction.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one exact side-correction cut and bound its allowed cost from a favorable completed moment at a declared target. Stop or hand off if the necessary source/target access cannot be justified or even the optimistic total misses the target.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.

actual_scope: Extend the P104 monotone relay floor to read-only access to every original G/Q/D value at its actual chronological frame, including unfinished source rows outside K.
scope_change_reason: PR2383 explicitly excludes unfinished original helper reads and asks whether they evade its quotient argument. The new finite endpoint-avoidance premise and coupled source-decomposition induction settle actual-frame read-only access without treating those rows as arbitrary-frame oracles.
bottleneck_link: This rules out harvesting the existing unfinished helper information for a free correction arrival while retaining the original word. A changed schedule or writable descending path must be named before building an escape.
stop_rule: Stop after the actual-frame helper-read implication and exact finite premises; do not synthesize a correction or infer a complete cost/supplier bound.
evidence: Written arbitrary-length proof; exact 280-input event replay and source decomposition at every modified non-target state; all104 endpoint/source-support/minor witnesses; semantic controls.
author: ywz65
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in derivation, implementation, checking and writing; no independent human or formal proof assistant review.

open_questions.question: Can one changed original helper path create a target-endpoint contact with useful outside-code source information?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Actual-frame read-only use of all current paths cannot evade the 208-lifetime floor.
open_questions.first_step: Select one original helper and endpoint, change its path explicitly, then check all retained captures/cleanup and price the newly required transports before synthesis.
open_questions.blocked_by: No unchanged helper visits any target endpoint; a new contact must preserve all existing source and query contracts.

open_questions.question: Can writing new information into an original descending private lifetime improve a completed correction?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The theorem assumes the original word remains read-only; source information outside K carried down would violate its invariant.
open_questions.first_step: Specify one new pre-descent update and the exact source projection after it, then derive chronological capture and dirty-restoration requirements.
open_questions.blocked_by: Native/physical legality, restoration and full paid moment are not supplied by a source-row escape.
